title: Low-Resource Language as a Shared Blind Spot: Correlated Safety Failures Across Models

original_idea.body:
# Low-Resource Language as a Shared Blind Spot: Correlated Safety Failures Across Models

**Problem:** Safety failures in low-resource languages are well known per-model, but the homogeneity link is whether ALL models share the SAME multilingual blind spot. If correlated, then a multilingual jailbreak is a universal key, and provider diversity offers no protection for non-English users — a diffuse, neglected harm.

**Direction:** Take a small set of harmful requests, translate into a few low-resource languages, and run across 5+ models. Measure per-language refusal/leak rates and, crucially, the CORRELATION of failures across models per language. Show whether models fail together in the same languages (shared blind spot) vs. independently.

**Why it matters:** If the multilingual blind spot is shared ecosystem-wide, it's a systemic safety gap for the global majority that no single lab is incentivized to fully close. Reframes a known per-model issue as a homogeneity/concentration problem. Cheap, inference-only.

**Relevant context:** Grounded in 'Global Security Blind Spots: LLM Safety Failures in Low-Resource Languages' and multilingual-jailbreak findings. Reframed through Artificial Hivemind correlated-failure lens (arXiv 2510.22954).
